note: Triennial election of Tyrone County Council, 1964. Nominations closed on 19 May 1964 and the Irish News reports no contests, the only newcomers being Mr. Jack Simpson (Castlederg) and Mr. James Donnelly (Donaghmore) (Irish News, 20 May 1964, p. 7). The Returning Officer's official notice of result, printed in the Strabane Chronicle of 30 May 1964, lists all 27 county electoral divisions and the elected member's surname. Given names are taken from the 1958 returning officer's notice where the same member continues, and from the 1964 and 1967 press reports; the 1964 notice itself prints surnames only. No poll took place; the round keeps the queue's statutory date, Thursday 4 June 1964, which no retrieved page states. Uncontested divisions here reflect a deliberate abstention, not missing coverage: in the Omagh Rural District, Nationalists refused to nominate against Unionist-held seats in every year except 1949, when only 4 of 21 such seats were contested (Kingsley 2021, 'The Omagh Rural District Electoral Divisions Scheme 1923', citing PRONI LA/62/2/FA/38 and Ulster Herald 10 Feb 1923). The same pattern is visible across this county's rounds. See notes/tyrone-county-council_absent_contests.txt The official notice prints the surname only ('PURDY'). Returned unopposed.
